If the value is handed over by reference rather than copied, document it read-only and pin that with a test, because the consumer that normalizes it is one in-place `.map` away from corrupting the producer's state.
rationale: #271: providers carry each commit's already-fetched diff on `GitCommit.diffs` so the sync loop stops re-requesting it. A merge commit whose diffstat 404s legitimately yields `[]`; treating that as falsy would have sent precisely those commits back to the endpoint that just 404'd — reinstating the duplicate request for the exact subset the change targeted. The array is also passed by reference, so the namespacing step had to keep mapping to new objects.

title: Cap unbounded request payloads and stored fields
rule: Set an explicit bodyLimit and per-field/byte caps on every authenticated write of unbounded content (ciphertext, JSON metadata, free-text ids) so an opted-in user cannot exhaust storage.
rationale: Recurred in #125 (ciphertext, encryption_meta, session_id, and tool had no size cap and no bodyLimit).

title: Chunking a window bounds the per-run peak but can multiply the total
rule: Before capping a re-fetch window into chunks, evaluate the RECOVERY path, not just the steady state or the failing state. Any sibling fetch in the same loop that is NOT bounded by the same cap re-runs in full once per chunk, so chunking multiplies its total cost by roughly (lag / (2 x cap)) even while the capped fetch's total stays flat. Chunking buys a bounded per-run PEAK, paid for with a higher TOTAL on every unbounded sibling — often the right trade for a rare one-off catch-up, but state it as a trade, and name in the docstring exactly which fetches the cap does and does not reach (including where a provider implements the bound client-side and so pays the full listing cost regardless).
rationale: #235: capping the git catch-up window at 30 days bounded the commit walk and its per-commit getCommitDiff fan-out, but getPullRequests takes no `until`, so each chunk re-listed every PR from its advancing `since` to now: a 200-day recovery went from 200 PR-days in one run to 200+170+140+110+80+50+20 = 770 across seven. Bitbucket compounded it — its getCommits pages from HEAD and filters `until` in memory, so a chunked recovery re-pages HEAD to since once per chunk.

title: Keep time scope consistent across one view
rule: Every figure rendered together must share the same time window; an all-time-computed badge over windowed metrics contradicts its column, so window it too or explicitly label it.
rationale: Recurred in #104 (computeTeamTiers was all-time while every metric in the column was scoped to [from,to]).

title: Dedupe at the write/aggregation layer, not via a UI contract
rule: When an append-only log must be deduped, enforce it at the writer or read-aggregation layer; do not rely on a UI/consumer component to prevent duplicate writes, since the endpoint is reachable directly.
rationale: Recurred in #162 (view-recording deduped only via a per-mount React ref, so the POST endpoint could append unbounded duplicate 'viewed' events).

title: Delete superseded routes, clients, and types when a feature replaces them
rule: When a new surface supersedes an old one, remove the now-orphaned routes, client methods, hooks, query keys, and types in the same PR, or explicitly document them as intentionally public.
rationale: Recurred in #132 (the unified manager panel repointed the UI but left the old per-pillar routes plus a dead client method/hook/queryKey/type behind).

title: Derive time-sensitive test fixtures from a frozen clock
rule: Any test whose fixture is computed from Date.now() inherits the wall-clock instant the suite happens to run at, and that leaks into the assertion in two ways: offsets that are exact multiples of 24h inherit the run's TIME-OF-DAY (so a fixture straddles a UTC day boundary near midnight), and back-to-back operations can share a millisecond (so two 'distinct' instants compare equal and a not-equal assertion turns vacuous or flaky). Freeze with vi.setSystemTime and step it explicitly; put vi.useRealTimers() in an unconditional afterEach. A test that passes at 12:00 and fails at 00:30 is worse than a missing test — it is green for every human who runs it by hand and red on every nightly CI cron.
rationale: #235: two tests. A streak test asserted since !== third-run instant, but three runs shared a millisecond and it failed live. A split-UTC-day merge test derived its chunk boundary from Date.now() with 24h-multiple offsets, so the boundary inherited the run's time-of-day; within an hour of UTC midnight a commit landed on an adjacent day and the assertion got 1 instead of 2 (reproduced at 00:30Z and 23:30Z) - ~8% of arbitrary runs but every night for a CET-based CI cron.

title: Don't bind provider semantics to exact UI-copy strings
rule: Extract provider verdicts from structured API fields, not by exact-equality matching on human-readable system-note text; if unavoidable, use a prefix match and pin the version verified.
rationale: Recurred in #123 (GitLab approvals were detected via body === 'approved this merge request', UI copy that drifts across versions).

title: Floor every individual-derived count and block differencing
rule: In manager/team aggregates, apply the k-anonymity floor to every count derived from individuals (including opt-in/eligibility tallies) and ensure org-vs-team panels cannot be differenced to isolate one person.
rationale: Recurred in #132 (opted_in_developers was unfloored and the explicit-0/null distinction let a manager difference org vs team panels).

title: Guard cache merges on a matching id
rule: When patching a cached entry via setQueryData, verify prev.id === id before merging derived fields, so a stale cache entry cannot receive another entity's data.
rationale: Recurred in #163 (useTogglePracticeFeedback merged feedback counts into practiceDetail(id) without a prev.id === id guard).

title: Idempotent upserts must preserve first-occurrence timestamps
rule: On conflict, an upsert for a detected/triage record must not overwrite the original detected_at/created_at; bumping it on every re-scan turns 'first detected' into 'last detected'.
rationale: Recurred in #102 (upsertAnomaly set detected_at=excluded.detected_at on conflict, erasing when an anomaly first appeared).

title: Never embed a raw control byte in source; write the escape
rule: A separator or sentinel that must not collide with real data should be written as an ESCAPE (\u0000, \0), never as a literal control byte pasted into the file. A single NUL makes git classify the file as binary, which silently disables core.autocrlf/.gitattributes EOL normalization and turns the next commit into a whole-file line-ending rewrite; it also makes ripgrep and most search tooling refuse the file, so the code becomes hard to review exactly where review matters most. The failure is invisible in an editor and fails OPEN — a formatter that strips control characters collapses the separator to the empty string.
rationale: #250: a NUL typed as the rawWrites dedupe separator made git treat sync.ts as binary. Its diff went from ~290 real lines to 3955 (a full CRLF rewrite that destroyed per-line blame on the epic's most safety-critical file), and grep over it returned truncated results. Three separate review findings traced to that one byte.

title: Normalize client-supplied timestamps to UTC ISO on ingest
rule: A timestamp accepted from a client must be canonicalized to UTC ISO at the boundary (new Date(x).toISOString()), not stored verbatim after a loose Date.parse non-NaN check, especially when an index sorts on it.
rationale: Recurred in #125 (captured_at passed only a Date.parse check and was stored raw, violating the UTC-ISO invariant).

title: Order specific rules before generic ones, and assert the reason not just the verdict
rule: In a chain of classification/matching rules where more than one can fire for the same input, put the SPECIFIC rule before the GENERIC one — a generic rule placed first shadows the specific one, silently making its lookup table or branch unreachable dead code. Test it by asserting WHICH rule fired (the reason/label), not merely the boolean verdict: a test that checks only the verdict still passes when the specific rule's whole data set is emptied.
rationale: #254: the generic bot-suffix rule ran before the known-bot-name rule, so stripBotSuffix was unreachable and every '*-bot' entry in KNOWN_BOT_LOGINS was dead. The it.each over known bots asserted only isBot, so it passed via the suffix rule and would have kept passing with the set emptied.

title: Keep cross-provider-normalized metrics symmetric
rule: When a metric is contracted as provider-agnostic, freeze durable derived facts consistently across providers (COALESCE-freeze merge timestamp/duration) so one provider's re-sync approximation doesn't drift while others stay exact.
rationale: Recurred in #123 (Bitbucket derived merged_at from updated_on, so post-merge comments inflated time_to_merge on Bitbucket only).

title: Test a merge/combine rule with discriminating inputs, not degenerate-equal ones
rule: A test of a combine rule (max, min, weighted average, first-observed) must use inputs that make the intended rule produce a value that plausible wrong variants would NOT. Equal/identical inputs (f(1,1), same rate on both sides) can't distinguish max from min from take-either, or a weighted mean from a plain mean. Bind a max/never-below-stored guard with stored != incoming (e.g. f(1,0)=1), discriminate commit-weighting with unequal counts AND unequal values, and prove a first-observed/frozen rule by delivering a different second value.
rationale: #205: the initial re-delivery test used stored==incoming==1, so Math.max was indistinguishable from min/take-incoming — a revert to take-incoming (the exact data-loss regression) stayed green; and an avg_commit_size assertion on equal inputs couldn't tell commit-weighting from a plain mean.

title: Test an order-independent selection with the winner out of positional-bug position
rule: When testing a max/min/newest selection across a collection, place the expected winner where a positional bug (take-first / take-last) would NOT pick it — e.g. list the newest element first when the code should pick the newest. Otherwise a `result = current` (take-last) mutant passes and the core comparison is unproven.
rationale: #246: the newest-cursor test seeded the winning (newest) cursor last in provider order, so it also passed against a broken take-last selection; reordering the winner to first pins the max comparison.

title: Validate URL scheme before rendering a stored string as an href
rule: A stored user-supplied URL rendered into an <a href> must be scheme-validated (new URL() + allowlist http/https) at the write boundary, and the renderer must neutralize non-http schemes to plain text; an opaque string href allows stored javascript:/data: XSS.
rationale: #150: outcomeLink was stored as an opaque string and rendered directly as <a href={outcomeLink}> with no scheme check — latent stored XSS once an authoring route can plant the value.
